{"filepath":"one_page_comparison.md","content":"# EV Connector Comparison for Fleet Buyers — One‑Page Brief

Prepared: 2026-09-06
Source: ev_connector_research.md (see cited sections below)

Executive summary & recommendation

For most commercial fleets outside mainland China, specify CCS (CCS1 in North America, CCS2 in Europe) as the primary DC charging standard today — it offers the widest vehicle compatibility, broadest public and private charging ecosystem, and best long‑term vendor support. Where your fleet operates primarily in North America and expects heavy Tesla/NACS vehicles, plan a CCS-first build with NACS adapter strategy or dual‑outlet chargers that support NACS as a future transition. For China operations, use GB/T. For Japan/legacy markets with heavy CHAdeMO presence, move toward ChaoJi/transition strategies. (Sources: ev_connector_research.md — "Combined Charging System", "NACS/Tesla", "GB/T", "CHAdeMO/ChaoJi").

Side‑by‑side (compact)

- CCS (CCS1/CCS2)
  - Pros: Widest OEM support, high deployed DC power (up to 350+ kW in deployment), strong public network presence.
  - Cons: Charging power varies by deployment; site electrical upgrades can be costly.
  - Best for: Mixed commercial vans, medium/heavy trucks (fast depot/public DC), pan‑regional fleets (NA/EU). (Source: "Combined Charging System")

- NACS (Tesla/NACS)
  - Pros: High adoption in Tesla-heavy NA markets; compact connector, strong reliability.
  - Cons: Limited native non‑Tesla vehicle support (adapter strategies required), evolving standardization and availability.
  - Best for: Tesla‑centric fleets or NA fleets with planned NACS transition. (Source: "NACS/Tesla")

- GB/T (China)
  - Pros: Required/ubiquitous in China; localized supply chain and cost advantages.
  - Cons: Not interoperable with CCS/NACS without adapters or dedicated hardware.
  - Best for: China‑based fleet operations. (Source: "GB/T")

- CHAdeMO / ChaoJi
  - Pros: Mature ecosystem in Japan; ChaoJi aims for higher power/interop.
  - Cons: Declining outside Japan; transition path needed. Best for Japan/legacy CHAdeMO vehicles. (Source: "CHAdeMO/ChaoJi")

Operational impacts (practical points)

- Charging speed & uptime: DC fast‑charging speeds depend on charger power, vehicle battery capability, and site power (deployed CCS stations commonly 50–350 kW; spec ceilings higher) — design chargers to match your fleet’s peak battery acceptance to avoid wasted capital. (Source: ev_connector_research.md)
- Adapters & interoperability: Adapters can bridge NACS↔CCS and GB/T gaps short‑term but add logistic/maintenance overhead and possible throughput limits; avoid adapter reliance for high‑duty applications. (Sources: "NACS/Tesla", "GB/T")
- Maintenance & reliability: Simpler connectors (NACS) can reduce mechanical failure points; networked CCS chargers often require firmware/OCPP management and periodic high‑voltage servicing. Budget for preventative maintenance and spare cables/CCS plugs. (Source: ev_connector_research.md)

Rough cost & installation considerations

- Charger cost scales with power: 50 kW DC ~ lower CAPEX per unit but higher per‑kWh charging time; 150–350+kW chargers cost more and require larger site power and transformer upgrades. Expect site electrical upgrades and demand charges to dominate early project costs. Include network/roaming fees and adapter purchase if needed. (Source: ev_connector_research.md)

5‑item procurement checklist

1. Confirm vehicle inlet(s) and max DC charge acceptance for your fleet (per vehicle model).
2. Specify primary connector by region (CCS for NA/EU, GB/T for China) and document adapter/transition plan.
3. Size site power to support peak simultaneous charging plus growth (include transformer/utility upgrade quotes).
4. Require vendor support SLAs, remote management (OCPP/telemetry), spare parts, and preventative maintenance plans.
5. Contractually lock interoperability, warranty terms, and upgrade/retrofit paths for alternative connectors (e.g., NACS adapters, ChaoJi-ready hardware).

Cited: ev_connector_research.md — sections "Combined Charging System (CCS1 / CCS2)", "NACS/Tesla", "GB/T", "CHAdeMO/ChaoJi", general notes."}
